text: Bevy 0.19.1 was released on 13 August 2026.
Bevy 0.20.0 was released on 8 October 2026, after release candidates on 15 and 28 September 2026.
The bavovniatko research pack targets Bevy 0.19 stable and keeps 0.19.1 pinned until the plugins it relies on support Bevy 0.20.
The bavovniatko world architecture is per-chapter dioramas of 10–100 km plus a 2D country map, not one continuous country-scale 3D world.
A 32-bit float has about 1.6 cm of resolution at 200 km from the origin, so diorama-local origins keep f32 transforms precise enough and floating-origin machinery is not a v1 dependency.

observations.subject: f32 resolution at 200 km from origin

text: No ready-made Bevy plugin exists for sensor looks (FLIR, night vision, FPV feed artefacts, radar scope); each is one fullscreen post-process system and shader.
In Bevy 0.19 render passes are plain ECS systems in the Core3d and Core2d schedules, which makes custom post-processing simple.

Bevy 0.19 renders large scenes GPU-driven: multi-draw indirect with GPU-side batch-set unpacking, GPU-checked visibility ranges, batched depth-only prepasses, sparse mesh-uniform uploads and GPU light clustering.
Bevy's large_scenes/bevy_city example generates 55,000 rendered entities by default.

observations.subject: rendered entities in the bevy_city example

text: Bevy 0.19 removed the old render graph; render passes are regular systems in Core3d/Core2d ordered with .before() and .after().
Bevy 0.19 added built-in Vignette and LensDistortion (barrel/pincushion) components, the base of an FPV-drone camera look.
Bevy 0.19 lighting adds contact shadows, physically based screen-space reflections, rectangular area lights, parallax-corrected cubemap probes and partial bindless rendering.
Bevy 0.19 carries a built-in Bruneton-style atmosphere (Atmosphere with a ScatteringMedium, AtmosphereEnvironmentMapLight, AtmosphereSettings) that bevy-aqua and bevy_weather use.
Bevy's atmosphere composites the sky between the opaque and transparent passes in physical radiance times camera exposure; bevy-aqua and bevy_weather both calibrate around EV100 12–13.
Bevy's built-in fog examples are distance fog, local fog volumes, volumetric fog, scrolling fog and atmospheric fog.
Volumetric fog in Bevy requires WebGPU on the web; WebGL2 cannot run it.
Solari, Bevy's real-time path-traced renderer, improved in 0.19 (temporal stability, mirrors, non-metallic materials) but is not needed for v1.
Bevy 0.19's BSN scene notation makes spawning large generated content far less boilerplate, though asset-driven .bsn loaders are still to come.
bevy-clipmap 1.0.5 (Bevy 0.19 per its README) renders one huge heightmap at adaptive LOD with Hoppe-style GPU geometry clipmaps and ships a Python 16-bit PNG to KTX2 pipeline.
bevy-clipmap's terrain self-shadowing horizon maps cost 360·W·H·4 bytes: 1.4 GB at 1k, prohibitive past about 8k.

bevytiles 0.1.0 (Bevy 0.19) is a geo-spatial tile-streaming engine with lat/lon world config, quadtree LOD, Terrarium heightmap decoding, CPU ground_height() queries, threaded tile fetch with disk cache and a TerrainAnchor rebase convention.
bevytiles streams Esri imagery and Mapzen/AWS terrain tiles whose terms must be respected; bavovniatko would use its architecture fed by its own baked tiles.
bevy_3d_tiles 0.4.4 streams OGC 3D Tiles (including Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles) on native and wasm, but crates.io lists it as preview only, so it is a reference rather than a dependency.
terraink 0.0.2 is a small Bevy renderer for DEMs (GeoTIFF, Terrarium PNG) and Mapbox vector tiles, a reference for a Copernicus GLO-30 ingest path.
bevy_mesh_terrain 0.15.11 (Bevy 0.15, lagging) offers chunked heightmap terrain with splat mapping, with companions bevy_regions and bevy_foliage_paint.
bevy_symbios_ground 0.5.0 is an active (Aug 2026) algorithmic terrain integration with small adoption.
bevy_a5 0.1.2 provides A5 geospatial pentagonal cells for floating-origin use and spatial queries.
Bevy 0.19's built-in examples cover per-mesh LOD swaps (visibility ranges, now GPU-checked), occlusion culling and meshlets.

bevy_feronia 0.8.4 is the strongest Bevy scatter system (declarative scatter layers, LOD-matched items, Ghost of Tsushima-inspired wind shaders, heightmap baking), but it pins Bevy 0.17, so its WGSL should be mined rather than depended on.
warbler_grass 0.6.1 is the classic dense GPU billboard grass for Bevy but targets Bevy 0.13/0.14 and is outdated.
bevy_procedural_tree 0.4.0 generates procedural 3D tree meshes, a candidate for oak, pine, poplar and birch shelterbelt variety.
Bevy 0.19's GPU-driven batching makes plain instanced-mesh vegetation viable at extreme counts.

bevy-aqua 0.1.3 (Bevy 0.19) is the most complete Bevy water stack: five displacement cascades, analytic or Tessendorf FFT waves, foam, a terrain bed for shoaling, bounded water bodies including rivers, GPU wave-query probes, reflections, caustics and underwater scattering.
bevy-aqua's GPU WaveQuery probes return 256 surface samples per frame with about one frame of readback latency, enough for buoyancy and sea-drone gameplay.

bevy-aqua's author documents one active Camera3d as the supported view path (multi-camera and picture-in-picture untested), one horizontal level per water body, and a known Bevy 0.19.1 planar-mirror normal bug.
bevy_water 0.18.1 (Bevy 0.18) is a long-lived tileable dynamic ocean material with get_wave_point() for floating objects, a camera-agnostic fallback where multi-view scenes break bevy-aqua.

For Snake Island and the Black Sea drone war, bevy-aqua's open ocean and underwater view fit the sea-drone POV; for the Kherson crossings and Krynky, its river corridor over a Dnipro bed heightmap fits.
notes: The block's only citation is bevy-examples-tree; the mapping is the pack's own design judgement.

text: Bevy's built-in transmission example covers shallow river refraction for minor streams without bevy-aqua.

bevy_weather 0.2 (Bevy 0.19) drives day and night from real solar geometry, wires Bevy's atmosphere, and draws stars, moon, raymarched volumetric clouds with cloud shadows, volumetric fog, GPU rain and snow, and lightning with speed-of-sound thunder delay.
bevy_weather's GroundConditions keeps persistent wetness and snow, which can model rasputitsa as data.
In bevy_weather, weather is a deterministic function of clock and seed, with forecast(), so the sky is the same after save/load and on every machine.
bevy_weather's quality tiers run from Potato to Ultra: cloud steps 12 to 128, light march 0 to 8 and particles 1,200 to 60,000.

observations.subject: cloud raymarch steps by quality tier

text: bevy-volumetric-clouds 0.2 (Bevy 0.18) implements Horizon Zero Dawn-style raymarched clouds but has its own simple sky, no depth-buffer integration and a fixed 1920×1080 render target.
bevy_fast_clouds (Bevy 0.19) renders wavelet-volume clouds that skip provably invisible work; it is very new (Sep 2026) with tiny adoption.
bevy_hanabi 0.19.0 (Bevy 0.19) is a GPU particle system suited to smoke columns, dust, artillery blooms and tracers, with a RON asset loader available.
bevy_stage 0.2.0, by bevy_weather's author, loads glTF levels with artist metadata, streaming sectors and LOD.

In bevy_weather's design, stars and moon are drawn in the opaque pass at the far plane with depth writes off, while clouds are drawn in the transparent pass after the atmosphere with their own aerial perspective, or overcast reads brighter than clear.
Bevy's sky renders for every 3D camera, so minimap and render-to-texture cameras must be scoped out with render layers.
bevy_weather advises fog visibility via DistanceFog with a matching sky fade toward colour, and handing the sun the raw solar spectrum, since pre-reddened light double-counts Rayleigh extinction.
big_space partitions the world into nestable integer grids for drift-free absolute coordinates with plain Transform compatibility; it has about 37,000 downloads.
big_space 0.13.0 for Bevy 0.19 and 0.14.0-rc.0 for Bevy 0.20 were released on 8 October 2026; on 2 October the latest release was 0.12 for Bevy 0.18.
big_space_solari resets ray-traced lighting history when a floating origin recentres, showing that recentring must reset temporal GPU effects.
chunky-bevy 0.18 provides simple chunk load-in/load-out management.
bevy_spatial 0.11 (Bevy ~0.16, lagging) tracks entities in KD-tree spatial indices for nearest-neighbour queries.
The utm 0.1.6 crate converts lat/lon to UTM in about 300 lines, MIT-licensed and no_std-capable.
Diorama-local origins make big_space unnecessary for v1; if dioramas later merge into one world, the temporal-effect reset must be budgeted.

Bevy 0.19.1's examples include split-screen viewports, render-to-texture composited into UI (the picture-in-picture drone-feed pattern), camera sub-views, orthographic and custom projections, and free, orbit and first-person camera controllers.
A per-camera post chain in Bevy 0.19 can combine Vignette, LensDistortion, colour grading, tonemapping, auto exposure, motion blur and a custom post-processing pass.
bevy_rts_camera 0.14 (Bevy 0.19, MIT/Apache) offers pan, zoom and rotate with ground-following, smoothing and edge pan.
milsymbol 0.3.0 is a native Rust port of milsymbol.js for MIL-STD-2525/APP-6 symbols, released in Sep 2026; milsymbol-rs instead wraps the JavaScript library.
bevy_geo_tiles 0.2.1 and bevy_map_viewer 0.2.1 render slippy-map raster tiles in Bevy.
evroon's bevy-adsb renders live ADS-B aircraft traffic in Bevy.
rusty-rotor, a work-in-progress Bevy FPV drone simulator, is the only FPV-drone prior art found for Bevy.
Every extra Bevy camera re-renders the scene it sees, so drone-feed views need render layers and low feed resolutions.

Digital Extinction, archived in 2024 and AGPL-3.0, is the most complete Bevy RTS (heightmap terrain, spatial index, pathfinding, minimap, multiplayer); its architecture can be studied but its code and assets must not be copied.
evroon/bevy-open-world collects Bevy demonstrations (OSM rendering, quadtree terrain, ADS-B traffic, a day/night globe, flight instruments) that its author says are not published crates.
iron-curtain (2026, GPL-3.0 with a modding exception) is a young Rust-native C&C-style RTS engine on Bevy.
rusty-rotor (2025, MIT) is a work-in-progress FPV drone simulator prototype in Bevy.
bevy-aqua, bevy_weather, bevy-clipmap, bevytiles, bevy_rts_camera, big_space, bevy_hanabi and utm are all MIT and/or Apache-2.0 licensed.
In Bevy 0.19's many_cubes benchmark, 1.6 million PBR cube entities went from 49.5 ms to 18.8 ms per frame with culling (116,000 in view), and from 93.1 ms to 41.2 ms unculled.

Nearly all of bevy_weather's cost is the per-pixel cloud raymarch, with broken skies the most expensive; its CPU-rebuilt cloud-shadow texture costs about 1.5 ms at 64, 6 ms at 128 and 20 ms at 256, spread over frames.
Searches found no thermal/FLIR or night-vision plugins for Bevy.
Esri imagery and Mapzen/AWS terrain tiles must not be shipped without checking their terms; CC BY land cover (WorldCover, Dynamic World, Hansen) and the Copernicus DEM with attribution are preferred.

text: The bavovniatko engine baseline rests on the Bevy 0.19 release notes, the 0.19.1 example tree and Bevy's release list.
bevytiles' TerrainAnchor pattern (absolute = user − world_offset) handles large worlds in Bevy 0.19 without a floating origin.
All the camera primitives a drone, AWACS and ground view need are in Bevy 0.19.1's example tree.
